our_argument_summary: WIN-023 verdict 'Unfalsifiable': the ~950 AD SAA formation date is adopted from published paleomagnetic literature (Campuzano 2019 SHAWQ2k, Tarduno 2015), not predicted; linking it to a preterist theological timeline (Revelation 20, 'Satan's little season' ~1000 AD) supplies no dome-derived mechanism or testable consequence. The verdict text adds a window analysis (historicist anchor band AD 1033-1380; ~950 falls outside it) plus a Poisson base-rate argument on SAA-like recurrences (~200-400yr per Hare 2018), and a standardized second paragraph asserting the claim fails the post-hoc test as a categorical assertion with no observable, with monitor.py containing no validation domain.

holes_found.description: SUMMARY-TABLE MISATTRIBUTION: the finding states the dome 'wrongly attributes the timing to Schumann resonance changes via an unfalsifiable ‘aetheric phase transition’'. The dome's CURRENT site does not say this anywhere for WIN-023. Live wins.html (fetched 2026-06-11) gives WIN-023 in full as: 'Result: SAA onset ~950 AD matches Satan's little season onset ~1000 AD in full preterist timeline.' No Schumann mechanism; no 'aetheric phase transition'. That quoted-looking phrase belongs to WIN-022/PROS-002 (NMP post-1990 'phase transition', 'aetheric vortex crossing a threshold'). Provenance trace: the clause entered the finding via the ISS-446 patch (2026-04-07, found_by curmudgeon-hol-taxonomy), whose description framed WIN-023 as 'Schumann resonance ~950 CE' with a '7.83 Hz observed vs 22 Hz dome prediction' context — language that matches the Schumann-cavity WINs (002/029/038), not WIN-023. Whether this was a conflation in that holistic review or tracked a since-removed older dome framing, the published row now attributes to the dome a mechanism its current site does not state. Our own detail fields (detail_claim/evidence/verdict, both TLDRs) never mention Schumann — a summary-vs-detail mismatch on the most-read surface. A defender quotes the live site against our table row: 'where do we say Schumann resonance changes? If they misquote our mechanism, why trust their statistics?' This is the 'claims about things the dome model doesn't actually say' category, in the summary table, with a reactive author in contact.
holes_found.recommendation: Rewrite the finding clause to track the detail fields and the live site. Suggested: '...the dome correctly identified a real paleomagnetic event, but adopted the date from published literature and linked it to a theological timeline (‘Satan's little season’ onset ~1000 AD, full preterist reading) — an unfalsifiable retrodiction with no dome-derived mechanism or timing prediction.' If anyone can produce an archived dome version that did state a Schumann mechanism for WIN-023, the old claim may be moved to a dated 'the dome formerly claimed' aside; it must not stand as a present-tense attribution.

holes_found.description: CARRY-OVER (c5 H2 / ISS-2499, closed-as-fixed but fix incomplete and now sharper): the patch added 'Crucially, ~950 AD falls outside this historicist band — it is not a valid selection within the window the dome constructs' but left the paragraph's closing sentence 'The dome's apparent ~50-year fit is selection of one recurrence inside a wide window, not a tight prediction.' These now contradict on the surface: the event is declared both NOT a valid selection within the window and a selection inside a wide window. Two secondary defects: (a) the Poisson figure (P≈0.58-0.82) is computed on the AD 1033-1380 band that the text itself says the event is OUTSIDE, so as deployed the base-rate number does not bear on the dome's actual hit; (b) 'the window the dome constructs' misattributes the band — WE constructed the historicist band from mainstream anchors; the dome's implicit target is the calendar millennium ~AD 1000.
holes_found.recommendation: Recast as an explicit disjunction. Either the defender insists on rigorous historicist anchors — then ~950 AD misses the AD 1033-1380 band entirely (an ~83-year miss to the nearest anchor, worse than the advertised 5%) — or the defender allows a loose window around the calendar millennium generous enough to include 950, in which case the window is ≥~480yr wide (e.g. AD 900-1380) and P(≥1 SAA-like recurrence) ≈ 0.70-0.91 under the same Poisson model, so a hit somewhere is unremarkable. Change the closing sentence to '...selection of one recurrence inside whatever window is drawn wide enough to count it, not a tight prediction', and change 'the window the dome constructs' to 'the window the defense requires'. Decider note: ISS-2499 was closed as fixed; this finding shows the fix half-landed — reopen or open a successor ISS.

holes_found.description: NEW PARAGRAPH INTERNAL TENSION (the +16% drift content): the standardized post-hoc paragraph asserts 'This is not a derived quantity that can be checked against measurement; it is a categorical assertion (theological, symbolic, or definitional) with no observable to confirm or refute' and 'no empirical measurement could distinguish a world where this claim is true from one where it is false'. But the WIN's empirical component — the ~950 AD formation date — IS a measured observable; our own detail_evidence cites Campuzano 2019 for exactly that measurement and calls the claim 'retrodiction dressed as prediction', and paragraph 1 spends ~1,400 characters statistically analyzing that observable. Retrodiction-of-a-measurement and no-observable-exists are different failure modes; asserting both invites the quote-mining attack: 'your evidence says the date is measured, your verdict says no measurement could bear on it — pick one.' The unfalsifiable element is the dome-ADDED content (the theological/aetheric timing link), not the date itself.
holes_found.recommendation: Add one qualifying sentence at the head of the second paragraph, e.g.: 'The empirical component here — that the SAA's reversed-flux patch emerged ~950 AD — is real and measured, but it is wholly borrowed from published literature; what the dome ADDS (the link to the preterist millennium) is the categorical assertion with no observable consequence.' Then the existing 'no empirical measurement could distinguish...' sentence should be scoped to 'the dome-specific component'. Small targeted edit; preserves the paragraph's standardized function.

stronger_arguments.description: The disjunction framing (hole 2's fix) is itself the strongest available version of the window argument: under the rigorous reading the dome MISSES, under the loose reading the hit is base-rate expected. Currently the text gets the pieces but not the either/or structure that makes it airtight.

The dome's own evolution notes ('Completely failed to mathematically reconcile SAA splitting or predictive tellurics', raw-text/06-evolution.txt:16) are already cited in detail_evidence but could be promoted into the finding to replace the removed Schumann clause — it is the dome's own admission that it has no working SAA mathematics, which is stronger than any mechanism attribution we could make.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome correctly points at a real, peer-reviewed paleomagnetic result: the current SAA's reversed-flux patch does date to roughly 950 AD (detail_evidence cites Campuzano et al. 2019, doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2019.01.050, and Tarduno et al. 2015, doi:10.1038/ncomms8865 — both DOIs re-verified via the doi.org handle API this run). The proximity of that date to the calendar millennium is also arithmetically true (wins.json WIN-023 detail_verdict_text: 1000-950 = 50yr = 5%).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Pointing at a published measurement after publication is adoption, not prediction (wins.json WIN-023 code_analysis.post_hoc=true, re-validated this run); the dome's own page states the match in one line with no derivation (live wins.html WIN-023, fetched 2026-06-11), no registration date, and no monitoring domain (live monitor.py, 39 domains, none for SAA formation). The theological anchor is non-unique (detail_verdict_text's four historicist anchors spanning AD 1033-1380), so the '5% miss' dissolves into either a clean miss of the rigorous band or a base-rate-expected hit in a loose one.

advocate_mode.best_defense: "The reviewers concede — citing their own preferred literature — that the SAA's reversed-flux patch emerged ~950 AD, and our full-preterist timeline puts Satan's little season onset at ~1000 AD. A 5% timing coincidence across a millennium, stated with zero fitted parameters, is better agreement than most globe retrodictions of geomagnetic events. And look at their rebuttal's quality: their summary table claims we attribute the timing to 'Schumann resonance changes via an aetheric phase transition' — we say no such thing; that language isn't on our WIN-023 at all. Their own verdict paragraph then says both that ~950 AD 'falls outside' their historicist window AND that it is 'selection of one recurrence inside a wide window'. If the reviewers misquote our mechanism and contradict themselves on their central statistical argument, why trust the rest of the row?"
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: All three legs of this defense are repaired by holes 1-3: remove the unsupported Schumann attribution (hole 1), restructure the window argument as an explicit disjunction (hole 2), and scope the no-observable language to the dome-added component (hole 3). After those edits the defense collapses to 'a 5% coincidence is impressive', which the disjunction argument directly answers.

Using the same quoted phrase in WIN-023's row attributes WIN-022's mechanism to a WIN where the dome states only a theological match — a defender can put our two rows side by side with the dome's two entries and show we transplanted the quote. The SAA-family rows (004/005/024/035/037) and Schumann-family rows (002/029/038) are otherwise mutually consistent with WIN-023's treatment: none of them claims the dome ties SAA FORMATION timing to the Schumann cavity.

quantitative_verification.computations: Recomputed in node this run: lambda=W/R; P=1-exp(-lambda). R=200: lambda=1.735, P=0.824; R=400: lambda=0.868, P=0.580. Matches published 0.58-0.82. Supplementary: a 480yr window (AD 900-1380, the loosest band that includes the event) gives P=0.699-0.909 — the figure recommended for the hole-2 disjunction fix.
quantitative_verification.discrepancies: None numerically. The structural problem (hole 2) is that the correct Poisson number is computed on a band the event is outside of — an argument-deployment error, not an arithmetic one.

deeper_analysis: This re-review was triggered by +16.3% detail_verdict_text drift since c5 (2026-06-02). The drift decomposes into three c5-issue fixes that all landed correctly in isolation (ISS-2498 Poisson parenthetical — verified numerically; ISS-2501 Froom 1948 citation for the historicist anchors — reasonable scholarly reference, print-only so unverifiable online, flagged as citations_unchecked; ISS-2499 'outside the band' sentence) plus the standardized post-hoc paragraph rolled out across 55 WINs. Two of the three findings this cycle are second-order effects of those patches: the ISS-2499 fix inserted the correct observation without reconciling the paragraph's pre-existing conclusion sentence, leaving a surface contradiction sharper than the original fuzziness it fixed; and the 55-WIN standardized paragraph, written for genuinely categorical claims (e.g. WIN-032 New Jerusalem axis), overstates when applied to a WIN whose core quantity IS a published measurement. The critical finding (Schumann misattribution) is older — it entered via the ISS-446 patch on 2026-04-07 and has survived three review cycles unchallenged, illustrating exactly the 'never assume the previous reviewer got it right' failure mode: c3 explicitly praised the clause as 'genuine analytical content'. I checked the dome's live site this run rather than trusting the mirror or prior cycles; the attribution is not there. Note ISS-2500 (Hare duplication, c5 H3) was wontfix'd with recorded rationale — honored, not re-raised. Severity calibration: the misattribution is 'critical' per the severity guide (claims about things the dome model doesn't actually say, on the most-read surface, with a reactive author in DM contact with the operator), even though the fix is a one-clause edit; recommended_action stays minor_edit because the row's core argument (post-hoc + unfalsifiable theological link) is sound and well-evidenced.
